questions.question_text: What is the definition of $1\text{ radian}$?

options.text: The angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length equals the radius.
The angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal to the diameter.
options.why: Used the diameter of the circle instead of the radius in the definition.

options.text: The angle subtended at the centre by an arc of length $1\text{ cm}$ in any circle.
options.why: Treated $1\text{ radian}$ as a fixed metric arc length regardless of radius.

options.text: The fraction of a circle obtained by dividing $360^{\circ}$ by $100$.
options.why: Arbitrarily divided a full turn into $100$ parts, giving $3.6^{\circ}$ per part instead of using an arc equal to the radius.

questions.solution_text: One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle when the arc length equals the radius ($l = r$).

questions.question_text:
An arc of length $18\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle $\theta$ at the centre of a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$.
What is the value of $\theta$ in radians?

options.why: Multiplied arc length by radius instead of dividing arc length by radius.
Divided radius by arc length instead of arc length by radius.
Appended $\pi$ to the numeric value when $\pi$ was not present in the lengths.

questions.question_text:
An arc of length $5\pi\text{ cm}$ is part of a circle with radius $10\text{ cm}$.
What is the central angle in radians?

options.why: Divided the radius by the numerical coefficient $5$ of the arc length, then appended $\pi$.
Multiplied the arc length by the radius.
Dropped $\pi$ from the numerator during the division.

questions.question_text:
In a circle of radius $r$, an arc has length equal to the diameter $2r$.
What central angle does this arc subtend in radians?

options.why: Assumed an arc equal to the diameter sweeps the entire circumference.
Treated the arc length as $1$ radius rather than $2$ radii.
